newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open little changed Thursday, floor sources said, with continued labor unrest in Colombia providing support.
Talks to end a strike by Colombia's main truck drivers' union remained deadlocked late Wednesday. The talks continued into the Wednesday night but there was no news yet on the outcome.
"With the tightness in supply and the strike in Colombia, I think the market could go up," one trader said.

New York arabica futures closed sharply higher bolstered by speculative and roaster amid the background of supply concerns. July closed 5.05 cents higher at 193.40 cents a lb after trading from 185.50 to 196 cents. Spot May gained 3.10 to 214.30, while the outer months gained 0.05 to 5.00 cents.
Technically, traders said July faced resistance at Wednesday's high of 196, followed by 199, a contract high set Monday. Support was noted at 193.00, and then at 190 and 185.50 cents.
LIFFE coffee futures were flat to slightly higher in subdued dealings early Thursday. At the midday break, July was unchanged at $1,665.
